source.author: hor
source.text: faenum habet in cornu, longe fuge; dummodo risum excutiat sibi, non hic cuiquam parcet amico et quodcumque semel chartis illeverit, omnis gestiet a furno redeuntis scire lacuque et pueros et anus.
source.text_original: 'faenum habet in cornu, longe fuge; dummodo risum  / excutiat sibi, non hic cuiquam parcet amico  / et quodcumque semel chartis illeverit, omnis  / gestiet a furno redeuntis scire lacuque  / et pueros et anus.'
source.text_english: He has hay on his horn; flee far away. So long as he can shake out a laugh for himself, he will spare no one here, not even a friend, and whatever once he has smeared on his pages, he will eagerly want to know all about, both boys and old women, as they come back from the bakery and from the lake.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: et nos saepe manum ferulae subtraximus, de nobis quoque dici potest: faenum habet in cornu, longe fuge.
reuse.text_original: et nos saepe manum ferulae subtraximus, de nobis quoque dici potest: faenum habet in cornu, longe fuge.
reuse.text_english: and we too have often drawn our hand away from the rod; it can also be said of us: he has hay on his horn, run far away.
